_description: Typical fixture: ground-floor renovation + two-storey rear extension, construction-management overlay. De-identified fictional data.

summaryParas: Jordan and Mia want to open up the dark, compartmentalised ground floor of their 1970s Stirling home and add a light-filled, two-storey rear extension for family living and a new main suite above. The brief is a warm, durable, low-maintenance home that sits quietly in its bushland setting and is comfortable year-round.
This brief captures the direction agreed at the Concept Presentation so everyone — client, designer and Blue Leaf — is working from one shared understanding before detailed design begins.
scopeIn: New two-storey rear extension: open-plan kitchen / living / dining at ground, main bedroom + ensuite + walk-in robe above.
Renovation of the existing ground floor: reconfigured entry, laundry/mudroom, powder room, and two children's bedrooms refreshed.
New covered alfresco connecting living to the rear garden.
scopeOut: Swimming pool and landscaping beyond the immediate alfresco apron — deferred to a later stage.
Detached studio / garage — excluded from this brief.

preferenceGroups.name: External
items: Fibre-cement cladding (horizontal profile) to the extension, with timber-look battens as a feature to the entry — warm but low-maintenance.
Dark, slimline-framed windows and doors; generous glazing to the north living zone.

preferenceGroups.name: Internal
items: Engineered oak / blackbutt-tone flooring through living areas; 2.7 m ceilings to the new ground floor.
Calm, neutral palette; honest materials (timber, stone-look benchtops, matte finishes).

preferenceGroups.name: Kitchen & wet areas
items: Walk-in butler's pantry; island bench as the social centre.
Ensuite with freestanding bath and a large walk-in shower; underfloor heating preferred (to be costed).

assumptions: Allowances are feasibility-level only and will be replaced by developed pricing at pre-construction.
Existing roof structure over the retained portion is assumed sound; subject to inspection.
Council and development-approval costs are excluded from the concept estimate.
decisions: Confirm the extension footprint against the concept estimate band before detailed design proceeds.
Confirm the designer engagement and the certification pathway (building consent route).
Confirm priority inclusions vs. deferred scope so the design is costed to budget.
nextStepsParas: The next paid step is the Pre-Construction / Developed Design & Specification agreement (PTSA). From that point Blue Leaf develops the design with the consultants, locks the specifications and selections, and produces developed pricing — the point at which this preliminary brief becomes a detailed, costed scope.

actions: Confirm the certification pathway (building consent route) before working drawings proceed.
Size the north living glazing for passive solar and design the eaves / shading to suit (WN-01).
Coordinate the living-room steel opening with the façade glazing module (EX-01 / WN-01).
Confirm underfloor-heating inclusion to the ensuite so it can be coordinated with the slab and services.
purposeParas: Issued to Harper Reece Architecture (Alex Harper) to progress the developed design of the rear extension and ground-floor renovation. Latest basis: Concept Set C-02, issued 28 Oct 2026. This brief separates confirmed client requirements from indicative preferences, and lists the items needing design coordination.

North-facing living glazing for passive solar; eaves / shading to be designed to suit.
Minimum ground-floor ceiling height 2.7 m to new work.

Freestanding bath to main ensuite; butler's pantry to kitchen.
